kicad_symbol_note: Interface_UART:THVD1420D extends MAX481E (SOIC numbering: 1 RO, 2 RE, 3 DE, 4 DI, 5 GND, 6 A, 7 B, 8 VCC), which is the same numbering as the DRL package (ds p3); usable after checking the footprint field

circuit.role: R output isolation from the shared bench line [this design]
surge protection as in TI's example: series 10 ohm pulse resistors

supplies.note: figures are the VCC = 5.5 V rows, no load

logic: RE has a 2 M pull-up, DE a 2 M pull-down (p3): unconnected = everything off. Bus pins +-12 kV IEC contact (p1).
placement: At the bench header next to the CAN transceiver; A/B as a pair.
notes: RE/DE tie: electrically it is the normal half-duplex hook-up (receiver off while driving, so no echo). HERE IT IS NOT FINE: with RE tied to DE the receiver is ON whenever BENCH4 is low, so R would drive BENCH3 all the time the port is used for anything else, fighting the level shifter. Keep DE on BENCH4 and give RE its own expander line (default high = receiver off). With RE high and DE low the chip is in shutdown at 0.1 uA.
While RS-485 is in use the level shifter must not drive BENCH3 towards the brain (set the odd group to A->B or OE off).
unverified: Behaviour of D/DE inputs when VCC is switched off while the brain drives them (needed if +3V3_BENCH is gated).
